verdict.reasoning: Patient reports decreased hearing on the left and numbness around the left ear and jawline: "Just one side, just on my left side, I've noticed that the hearing's kind of gone down a bit" and "again it's the left side, it's kind of like around my left ear, and kind of, along here. So like, my jawline's just all feeling a bit numb round here."

Patient notes intermittent ringing and dizziness when it occurs: "I think, occasionally noticed a, ringing in my ear" and later "because of all the kind of, these symptoms I've been getting, especially sometimes when I get a ringing, I can feel a bit dizzy."

Denials of limb weakness, swallowing, speech, vision changes, ear pain, discharge, and fever are documented, but pruritus (itchiness) is not answered: "Do you have any itchiness in the ear?" is followed by no patient response. Thus it is incorrect to say she denies pruritus.

Patient states: "I've got kind of, been told I have polyps in my nose" and "they said, ages ago, I had something called, can't quite remember but, labyrinthitis, something like that, but again, nothing, nothing ongoing."

She uses a nasal spray as needed and does not recall its name: "I only take the, spray for my nose when I need it" and "Do you remember the name of the spray, at all?" / "Unfortunately I don't, sorry."
Patient says: "Um, that, that's all fine and, you know I take a Rennie's if I need to" and later: "sometimes take like Rennies, but I just get that from the chemist."
Allergy documented: "Do you have any , any allergies to any medication?" / "Uh, no just Latex."
Family history: "My brother had, Neurofibromatosis, I think it is. Um, other than that everyone else is OK."

Social history: "Yeah, so I'm a, I'm a jockey" and "I've just had to do far less training" and regarding home: initially "do you live alone?" / "Yeah, yeah." then clarified "Um, I, uh, live with my partner." and later "No, no pets."

Symptoms are left-sided, and clinician suggests Bell’s palsy and further evaluation for other causes: "what you're, what you're describing might be something called Bell's Palsy" and he also plans neurologic exam and to "have a look inside the ear" for other pathology.

Patient explicitly expresses anxiety about seriousness and death: "'cause I can panic and you can look online, get a bit, frantic" and "Hopefully nothing , so serious I will die from it, I don't know I just, I think got myself in a pickle."

Doctor arranges same-day in-person GP assessment for neurologic and ear exam: "I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today" and "we can do a, a what we call a, a neurological examination" and "Have a look, have a look inside the ear."

Plan involves admin booking and patient calling support number after 5 minutes: "I'm gonna send a message to our admin team, I'll ask them, to book you in for a face-to-face appointment" and "you can ring the , the support team number, I'll leave that number in your notes. And you can ring them after five minutes, and then they'll slot you in to a place that's convenient for you."

Doctor reassures condition is not life-threatening and emphasizes attending today: "this doesn't seem to be you know, anything um, that you're gonna die from" and "preliminarily I can, I can reassure you" and "in order to definitively reassure you, I, I think you need a physical examination today" and "please make sure the appointment gets done today."
